title: Microsoft 365 Copilot: Agent 365 Business Analytics for AI spend, usage and value
summary: Hold: the spending-control automation only lists policies; it cannot set spending limits or billing. The licensing field also reports entitlement as unpublished despite the documented Copilot licence prerequisite, and the Viva access-control path stops before the feature and access-setting choices.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans one place bringing AI spend, usage and value together for investment decisions.
claims.quote: Agent 365 Business Analytics brings AI spend, usage, and value together in one place, helping leaders understand where AI investment is going, what value it’s delivering, and where to invest next.

claims.claim: The planned experience explores cost across services, models, agents and users.
claims.quote: Explore cost across services, models, agents, and users

claims.claim: The roadmap describes understanding business use cases and the value AI creates.
claims.quote: understand the business use cases AI supports and the value it creates

claims.claim: The planned experience forecasts future spend.
claims.quote: forecast future spend to make more informed investment decisions.

claims.claim: Learn documents Business Analytics as a Frontier preview rather than a final design.
claims.quote: This feature is part of the Frontier preview program.

claims.claim: Frontier provides early access to Microsoft's AI innovations.
claims.quote: Frontier connects you directly with Microsoft's latest AI innovations. Frontier previews are subject to the existing preview terms of your customer agreements.

claims.claim: Preview availability and capabilities might change.
claims.quote: As these features are still in development, their availability and capabilities might change over time.

claims.claim: The dedicated app is aimed at business decision makers and general managers.
claims.quote: Business Analytics is a dedicated app for business decision makers and general managers (GMs) to view and track the cost and usage of their organization's Microsoft AI services in one place.

claims.claim: The app has Overview, Use cases, Cost & forecast, Users & groups and service pages.
claims.quote: Overview | How is my organization using AI, what is it costing, and what needs my attention?

claims.claim: The app combines licensed Microsoft 365 Copilot with usage-based services including Cowork, agents and GitHub Copilot.
claims.quote: brings insights for licensed Microsoft 365 Copilot and usage-based AI services, such as Copilot Cowork, agents, and GitHub Copilot, together in a single experience.

claims.claim: Cost & forecast focuses on usage-based billing and excludes Microsoft Copilot user subscription licence costs.
claims.quote: The Cost & forecast page focuses on usage-based billing. Microsoft Copilot user subscription license costs aren't included.

claims.claim: The Overview service cost for Microsoft 365 Copilot is shown as Included in license.
claims.quote: For Microsoft 365 Copilot, cost shows as "Included in license" because it's covered by the per-user license.

claims.claim: Forecast options include base and growth forecasts.
claims.quote: Base or steady forecast, which assumes future usage is consistent with recent usage.

claims.claim: What-if forecasting includes spend-cap and model-mix scenarios.
claims.quote:
Spend cap: Estimate the impact of applying a monthly spending cap
Model mix: Estimate the impact of shifting usage between models or providers

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: A reporting budget target does not create or modify a spending policy or enforce a spending limit.
claims.quote: A reporting budget target helps you analyze spending. Creating the target doesn't configure a spending policy or enforce a spending limit.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: A scenario changes only the forecast comparison, not live policies, limits, budgets, routing or access.
claims.quote: A scenario changes only the forecast comparison. It doesn't modify live access, model routing, spending policies, budgets, or user limits.

claims.claim: AI value estimates labour value rather than realised savings.
claims.quote: AI value is an estimate of the labor value associated with AI's contribution. It doesn't represent realized cost savings, increased revenue, or a guaranteed return on investment.

claims.claim: The app provides AI-cost views by user, group and model alongside value metrics where available.
claims.quote:
Which services, models, groups, or job functions are driving changes in cost?
The Users tab shows people who have an assigned usage limit.
AI value, when available

claims.claim: Some people receive access automatically in the documented preview.
claims.quote: Some people get access to Agent 365 Business Analytics automatically. Others need a Global admin to assign it.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated the app's general availability arrival/default behaviour, distinguished from preview access.
claims.quote: Searched: "Agent 365 Business Analytics" "general availability" default rollout; read roadmap, introduction, manage/introduction and Viva dashboard settings. Preview access is documented; no GA rollout/default statement found.

claims.claim: Permission sets, partitions and access policies let administrators determine capabilities and whose data users can see.
claims.quote: A permission set defines what users can do in the app, such as view dashboards and reports, export data, view identifiable data, customize reports, and publish reports.

claims.claim: Administrators can change time and hourly-rate assumptions that affect AI-value estimates.

claims.claim: No PowerShell or API for Business Analytics access policies is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Agent 365 Business Analytics" access policies permission sets PowerShell Graph API. Read manage/access, manage/introduction, Viva feature-access-management and manage-access-policies; found UI policy management and general VFAM, not an app access-policy API.

claims.claim: Settings > Viva > Settings > Manage feature access > Create a policy reaches the Viva Insights web app on/off control.
claims.quote:
Name the policy and select the app and feature for which you'd like to set the policy.
Select the Access setting option and choose On or Off to enable or disable the feature.
claims.fix: Extend the UI path and rendered row to 'Settings > Viva > Settings > Manage feature access > Create a policy > app and feature > Access setting > On or Off'. In the note, specify selecting the Viva Insights web app feature. The present path stops before the feature choice and the control; these steps are documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/viva/control-access-admin-center.

claims.claim: The printed Add-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy call disables the Viva Insights web app for everyone in the tenant.
claims.quote:
Example: Turn off the Viva Insights web app for all users in your tenant
ModuleId : VivaInsights
FeatureId : Viva Insights web app
Name : DisableFeatureForAll
IsFeatureEnabled : false
Everyone

claims.claim: The documentation does not unambiguously confirm that this particular Viva Insights web app feature ID disables Business Analytics.
claims.quote: Searched: "Business Analytics" "Viva Insights web app" FeatureId; "Agent 365 Business Analytics" "FeatureId". Read manage/introduction, VFAM and dashboard settings: VFAM is linked for app on/off, but settings apply only 'where applicable'; no explicit ID-to-app statement.

claims.claim: Microsoft says the documented Viva feature access controls are unavailable in GCC High and DoD.
claims.quote: The access controls described in this document aren't available in GCC-High or DoD. For GCC (Government Community Cloud), see the documentation for your specific app for availability.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not explained Business Analytics control behaviour in the government clouds listed on the roadmap.
claims.quote: Searched: "Agent 365 Business Analytics" "GCC" controls. Read VFAM cloud exclusion and Business Analytics introduction, manage/access and configurations; no Business Analytics-specific government-cloud control behaviour found.

claims.claim: Copilot > Cost Management > Get Started is the documented entry to configure Copilot Credits spending limits and billing.
claims.quote:
go to Copilot and then the Cost Management node.
To unlock AI experiences enabled by usage-based billing, select Get Started.
claims.fix: Extend the path to 'Copilot > Cost Management > Get Started > Activate the default spending policy for your organization > Set the monthly spending limit for this policy > Limit monthly spending'. The omitted panel/section headings and final option are on the cited setup page. Keep billing-method configuration described in the note rather than implying Get Started itself sets a limit.

claims.claim: GET /beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies is automation that sets the spending limits and billing described by the row.
claims.quote:
List spendingPolicies | GET /copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies | Get a list of spending policies.
Update spendingPolicy | PATCH /copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/{id} | Update a spending policy.
claims.fix: Replace the call with 'PATCH /beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/{id}' and its docs link with https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/api/admin-settings/cost-management/spendingpolicy-update; cite that reference. Add to the note: 'For existing policies, request-body periodLimit and perUserLimit set limits; billingMethods changes funding. Adding pay-as-you-go funding requires a complete billingInstrument; replacing an already-pay-as-you-go instrument is not supported.' The update reference and spendingPolicy resource reference document these properties and restrictions.

claims.claim: Creating a spending policy requires Global administrator or Billing administrator.
claims.quote: Creating a spending policy also requires the Billing Administrator or Global Administrator directory role at runtime.

claims.claim: The cited Cost Management API is a beta API.
claims.quote: APIs under the /beta version are subject to change. Use of these APIs in production applications is not supported.

claims.claim: The Cowork Value metrics toggle is reached through Manage > Configurations > Metric calculators > Cowork assisted hours and value > Edit calculator > Value calculator > Value metrics.
claims.quote:
Under Cowork assisted hours and value, select Edit calculator.
Select the Value calculator tab.
On the right, use the Value metrics toggle to turn AI value metrics on or off for your organization.

claims.claim: The tenant-wide Cowork value-metrics display setting is off by default.
claims.quote: Administrators can control whether AI value metrics for Cowork are displayed to users in their organization. This setting applies across the tenant and is turned off by default.

claims.claim: Viva Insights administrators can configure Cowork value metrics.
claims.quote: Viva Insights admins can configure Cowork value metrics.

claims.claim: Copilot value metrics require Global admin or both Viva Insights admin and Chief officer, as the body clarifies.
claims.quote: Only users who have both Viva Insights admins and Chief officer roles, or who are global admins, can configure Copilot value metrics.
claims.fix: Replace the ambiguous role sentence in controls[3].note and the rendered row with 'Viva Insights admins configure Cowork value metrics; Copilot value metrics require both Viva Insights admin and Chief officer roles, or Global admin.' The body already states the qualification correctly.

claims.claim: No PowerShell or API for Business Analytics metric calculators or value-metric display is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Agent 365 Business Analytics" metric calculators privacy minimum group size API PowerShell. Read configurations, manage/introduction, VFAM and manage-access-policies; no automation for these app calculators or the Cowork Value metrics toggle found.

claims.claim: Minimum group size is reached in Business Analytics through Manage > Configurations > Privacy > Minimum group size.

claims.claim: The minimum group size setting accepts a value of at least five and hides smaller aggregated groups.
claims.quote: Minimum group size is the minimum number of people that must be in a group before aggregated insights are shown. Enter a value of at least 5.

claims.claim: The minimum group size threshold does not apply to nonaggregated user-level insights.
claims.quote: It doesn't apply to user-level insights that aren't aggregated.

claims.claim: No PowerShell or API for Business Analytics privacy settings is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Agent 365 Business Analytics" metric calculators privacy minimum group size API PowerShell. Read configurations and Viva dashboard settings (including minimum group size), VFAM and manage-access-policies; no privacy/minimum-group-size setting API found.

claims.claim: No read page names a Business Analytics-specific VFAM feature ID.
